# Delivery and landed cost

Every [Offer](../reference/glossary.md#term-offer) gets two answers for the [Destination](../reference/glossary.md#term-destination): `shipping.delivery` says whether and how it arrives, and `landed_aud` says what `qty` units cost delivered. Comps and diagnostics get neither.

## Delivery status

`shipping.delivery_basis` states in words what the status rests on.

| `delivery` | Applies to |
| --- | --- |
| `direct` | `ebay_au` items for which eBay lists a shipping option to the postcode. `amazon_au`, `woolworths`, `coles`. `ozbargain` deals whose title says "Delivered". `facebook` listings that offer shipping. |
| `pickup` | `gumtree`, `facebook`, `aldi`. Drop these with `include_pickup: false`. |
| `via_forwarder` | `taobao`, `tmall`, `1688`, `jd`, `pdd`. Sellers ship within China only. |
| `no` | `cheapies`, which lists New Zealand retailers. |
| `unknown` | The source does not say. |

For `amazon_au`, `woolworths` and `coles` the status is a rule for the whole marketplace. The server does not check the delivery area of one item or one postcode, and `delivery_basis` says so.

Offers with `delivery: no` are left out of the result. The server counts them in one `not_deliverable` diagnostic for the marketplace.

## Landed cost

`landed_aud` is the total for `qty` units. `landed_breakdown` lists its parts, and `landed_basis` says how firm the total is.

| `landed_basis` | Formula | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `exact` | `price_aud * qty + shipping.cost_aud` | The source stated a shipping cost. |
| `exact` | `price_aud * qty` | A pickup listing. |
| `item_only` | `price_aud * qty` | The source stated no shipping cost, so the total leaves it out. |
| `estimated` | The forwarder estimate below | The delivery status is `via_forwarder`. |

An offer with no AUD price has no `landed_aud`.

## Forwarder estimate

A [Forwarder](../reference/glossary.md#term-forwarder) receives goods in China and ships them to Australia. The server estimates that cost from a rate per kg:

**Forwarder estimate**

```text
freight  = max(FORWARDER_MIN_CHARGE_AUD, weight_kg * qty * FORWARDER_RATE_AUD_PER_KG)
subtotal = goods + China domestic leg + freight
fee      = subtotal * FORWARDER_FEE_PCT
gst      = (subtotal + fee) * GST_RATE
landed   = subtotal + fee + gst
```

`weight_kg` is the `est_weight_kg` argument, or `FORWARDER_DEFAULT_WEIGHT_KG` when the search gives none. Search results carry no weight.

With the default settings, 10 units at 20 CNY each and 0.3 kg each cost:

| Part | Calculation | AUD |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `goods` | 20 × 0.215 × 10 | 43.00 |
| `china_domestic` | none stated | 0.00 |
| `forwarder_freight` | max(15, 0.3 × 10 × 12) | 36.00 |
| `forwarder_fee` | 79.00 × 0.0 | 0.00 |
| `gst` | 79.00 × 0.10 | 7.90 |
| `landed_aud` |  | 86.90 |

> [!WARNING]
> **Placeholder rates**
>
> The default rate of 12 AUD per kg, the 15 AUD minimum and the 0.5 kg weight are placeholders. An `estimated` total can be far from what you pay. Set the rates from your forwarder's rate card before you compare Chinese offers with Australian ones.
